summary: Candidate 3 closes both candidate-2 specialty-6 findings. Agent and human identity is exactly (kind, stable reviewerId), so provider, requested/resolved model metadata, request mode, and prompt/response path changes do not create independence. Model-assisted identity is exactly (kind, nonempty provider, nonempty resolved responseModel); requestedModel is never used as an identity fallback. All completeness/blind/comparator/verifier pairwise role checks use this key. The remaining boundary is only truthful attribution of declared identities and runtime-returned provider/model tags during the actual dispatch and handoff.

verifiedControls.control: Stable agent/human identity ignores mutable lane metadata
verifiedControls.evidence: docs/qa/implementation-readiness/correctness-audit/methodology.md:144 defines agent/human identity as (kind, stable reviewerId). scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:644-655 implements that exact key without provider, model, request mode, run, prompt path, or response path. The focused full-chain probe changed those fields and used distinct prompt/response paths while reusing one stable reviewerId; completeness/blind, blind/comparator, and comparator/verifier combinations were each rejected for both kind=agent and kind=human with exactly the intended independence failure.

verifiedControls.control: Model identity uses provider plus resolved responseModel only
verifiedControls.evidence: scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:648-654 uses provider and responseModel and never reads requestedModel. A schema-valid full-chain model probe used different reviewerId, requestedModel aliases, request modes, and prompt/response paths with the same provider and resolved responseModel; it was rejected solely because completeness and blind identities were equal.

verifiedControls.control: Empty model provider and resolved model fail closed
verifiedControls.evidence: scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:710-720 explicitly rejects empty model provider and responseModel. The reviewer definitions in packet-completeness-review.schema.json:135-188 and the corresponding blind, comparison, and result schemas require nonempty provider and responseModel. The focused probe independently exercised all four reviewer schemas and validate_reviewer(); every empty provider and empty responseModel case was rejected. With an unresolved responseModel, reviewer_identity returned (..., null) for both requested aliases, proving there is no alias fallback even before schema rejection.

verifiedControls.control: All role/lane pairings use the stable identity key
verifiedControls.evidence: scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:1450-1456 checks completeness versus blind; 1694-1722 checks comparator versus blind and completeness; 1843-1879 checks each verifier versus comparator, blind, and completeness. Focused full-chain mutations reproduced rejection at each boundary for both agent and human identities.

verifiedControls.control: Resolved model declaration is bound to the raw runtime envelope
verifiedControls.evidence: scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py:676-695 requires the closed successful model-response envelope, and 748-778 requires provider, requestedModel, responseModel, reasoning, prompt path, and prompt hash to equal the sealed reviewer declaration before returning the substantive review payload. The 92-control suite includes response-envelope and model-provenance drift rejection.

runtimeAttributionBoundary.conclusion: No further mechanical identity issue was reproduced. The validator proves consistency and declared-role separation, not personhood or truth of orchestration attestations. During actual execution, the integrator must reconcile the declared kind/stable reviewerId with the real Hermes subagent or human, and reconcile provider/responseModel with the actual runtime response. Relabeling kind/reviewerId or falsely attributing a response envelope remains outside artifact-only proof and is the sole residual identity boundary.
mechanicallyEnforced: agent/human identity equality by kind plus stable reviewerId only
model identity equality by nonempty provider plus nonempty resolved responseModel only
runtimeEvidenceStillRequired: actual Hermes subagent or human corresponding to each declared kind and stable reviewerId
no kind or reviewerId relabeling across assigned roles
actual provider and resolved responseModel returned by the runtime

testsRun.result: PASS: 0 failures; 140 manifest/progress units; all 140 pending-blind-derivation

PASS: six agent/human full-chain metadata/path reuse mutations were rejected at all role boundaries; same resolved model with different aliases/paths was rejected; empty provider/responseModel was rejected by all four schemas and validate_reviewer

residualRisks: Artifact validation cannot establish that a declared reviewerId, kind, provider, or resolved responseModel truthfully identifies the actual runtime actor; the final integrator must reconcile those values with dispatch/return records.
